text:
maria gonzalez: Heads-up — I'm starting a staggered driver + CUDA rollout for Dedicated pools in us-west-2 and eu-central tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Target stack: NVIDIA driver 545.102, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.19. Canary will be 5 A100 nodes (~2% of capacity).

jon li: thanks. timeline + rollback plan?

maria gonzalez: plan in short:
- canary: 5 nodes in us-west-2 A100 pool at 03:00 UTC for 30m monitoring
- phase 1: 20% of A100s + all H100 test pool (non-prod) after successful canary
- phase 2: remaining A100s + cross-region spots next 24h
- rollback: automated if error-rate > 1% or kernel oops / OOM spikes

sasha ivanov: what metrics will auto-trigger rollback?

maria gonzalez: 
- driver/kern logs: any 'kernel panic' or 'GPU reset' counts
- NCCL errors: repeated TIMEOUT or UNREACHABLE on >3 collective ops in 10m
- pod term rate: >1.0 per 1000 pods/min in affected nodes
- infra alert: node reboot within 10m of driver install

priyanka rao: add perf regression threshold: 15% tail latency increase for p95 token gen (redwood-api route). If seen, pause rollout and triage.

jon li: who runs the manual rollback? ops_oncall or infra?

maria gonzalez: ops_oncall will hit the automated rollback first (we'll flip the canary label to old driver image); infra team does manual node repro if automation stalls. commands below for rollback quick ops:
```
# mark canary nodes unschedulable for new-driver plan
kubectl label nodes -l rollout=dedicated-canary rollout-phase=old --overwrite
# drain and install old driver (example)
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l rollout=dedicated-canary -o name); do kubectl cordon $n; kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; ssh $(basename $n) 'sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced'; kubectl uncordon $n; done
```

sasha ivanov: noted. make sure we have node images pinned — last time kernel module mismatch caused SIGBUS after CUDA upgrade.

maria gonzalez: corrected: we'll pin kernel headers and driver package hashes in the RPM repo. Also will run DKMS check pre-install: `dkms status` and `modinfo nvidia` post-install.

devops-bot: Canary deployment started at 1752100001, nodes targeted: a100-canary-0..4, job_id=drv-roll-17521

ops_oncall: seeing one node with repeated 'GPU reset detected' logs in canary-2, pushing GPU health snapshot now.

maria gonzalez: can you paste the snippet?

ops_oncall: ``
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31,0xFFFFFFFF,0x00000000
``

priyanka rao: Xid 31 indicates a channel timeout on some kernels. We should check PCIe link state and firmware on that board. Is this an A100 PCIe or SXM?

ops_oncall: A100-SXM. No fw update pending. Single node so far.

maria gonzalez: pause phase. devops-bot — pause rollout and mark canary nodes cordoned.

devops-bot: Rollout paused at 1752100120, canary nodes cordoned.

jon li: let's not escalate region-wide yet. Quick checklist:
- capture dmesg + nvidia-smi -q
- try repro by running NCCL tests (collectives) on the node
- verify kernel module version: `modinfo nvidia | grep version`

sasha ivanov: I'll spin a diagnostic job to run nccl-tests and a synthetic token-gen workload to check for tail latency regressions.

maria gonzalez: thanks. If repro holds, plan B is to revert driver on canary nodes to 535 and re-run a narrower CUDA 12.2 build with different NCCL flags. We'll preserve logs under s3://redwood-infra/rollouts/1752100001/.

priyanka rao: cost note — keeping canary nodes cordoned will reduce capacity for Dedicated customers in us-west-2 by ~3% during business hours. We should communicate to sales if this extends >2h.

maria gonzalez: will notify sales and CS if >2h. ETA for initial triage 30m.

ops_oncall: uploaded gpu-health.tar.gz to the s3 bucket, link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-infra/rollouts/1752100001/gpu-health.tar.gz

jon li: good. keep thread updated with next steps. Once we have repro / no-repro we decide green path vs rollback fully. :thumbsup:

maria gonzalez: updating status: diagnostic run shows two failed NCCL collectives on canary-2, logs point to driver kernel module error. Moving to revert on that node and re-run tests. Will post results here.

devops-bot: Node canary-2 driver rolled back to 535 at 1752100365, health checks scheduled.

maria gonzalez: preliminary: reverted node stabilized, no further GPU resets. Keeping rollout paused until infra and hw-firmware teams confirm this isn't a wider issue. Closing updates for now.
